CR5-B01.title: SP-168 completeness FAILS — naming authority returns by omission
CR5-B01.mechanism: §2.0.1's four rows invoke only 19 of the document's 111 normative clauses. SP-167 fixes the requirement set at all 111; SP-169 confines failed sets to INVOKED requirements. Roughly 92 requirements are therefore permanently unfailable — among them SP-025 (Entry immutability), SP-043, SP-045, SP-071, SP-075, SP-160, SP-163 and SP-174.

constructions_one_per_element_class.begin: B′ cannot record the originating DaySlot ordinal — the member SP-019 gained under CR4-09 and SP-075 obliges. It honours SP-030/031/037/038, so its failed set is EMPTY and SP-150 compels ADMITTED.
constructions_one_per_element_class.record: C′ orders by wall clock and cannot produce a total order on timestamp collision (SP-045, invoked nowhere). Failed set empty. P-L1-A seals '+ canonical ordering'.
constructions_one_per_element_class.complete: D′ compacts and rewrites completed Entry content (SP-025, invoked nowhere) while satisfying every clause in the row at transition time.
constructions_one_per_element_class.boundary: R′ cannot preserve pending contributions across a restart. SP-156 compels ADMITTED and the row is 'n/a for failure', so divergence surfaces later as an untyped, mislocalized outcome mismatch at complete — while P-L1-B law 3 requires loss be TYPED.

CR5-B01.author_verification: CONFIRMED by recomputation. Union of the four §2.0.1 rows = 19 clause identities; 111 normative rows total; the remainder can never appear in any failed-requirement set.

CR5-B02.title: Clause identity under-distinguishes — the collision the calibration test was meant to catch
CR5-B02.mechanism: SP-170 is a NON SEQUITUR. INV-RC-KERNEL-4 forbids OVER-distinction ('no admitted construct may encode a distinction already encoded by another'); it is silent on UNDER-distinction. The author cited it as though it supplied injectivity in the needed direction. It does not.
CR5-B02.constructions: U′ (truncates content) and V′ (in-memory, non-durable) both fail ONLY SP-020 — four distinct obligations under one identity — so both publish {SP-020} and compare FULLY CONFORMING to each other, though V′ loses '+ durability', a P-L1-A sealed member. P′ and Q′ likewise collide on {SP-037}. The converse also fails: SP-022 and SP-032 co-encode one distinction, so identical substrates may publish {SP-022} versus {SP-022, SP-032}.
CR5-B02.significance: This is the founder's own calibration standard failing in both directions at once: the representation neither distinguishes everything RC-0001 cares about nor collapses what it does not.

CR5-B03.title: The T(A) self-reference hazard affects six of eleven docket items, not A-09 alone — and is worse than CR4-01
CR5-B03.mechanism: v0.5 states the limitation 'applies to A-09 alone among the eleven; the other ten are narrowed by SP-019's fact set or by source.' FALSE, and falsified by the document's own cross-reference columns. All six OPERATIVELY_DECIDED items — A-01, A-04, A-05, A-06, A-07, A-09 — have Y narrowed by an AUTHOR-PROPOSED clause, and in five of six the document's own Open-decision column names that item on that clause.
CR5-B03.author_verification: CONFIRMED by direct inspection of v0.5's metadata columns. SP-048 · AUTHOR-PROPOSED · Open-decision 'A-05, A-06' · self-described in its own text as 'an authored minimality choice, not a founder-sealed prohibition'. SP-130 · AUTHOR-PROPOSED · 'A-07'. SP-019 · AUTHOR-PROPOSED/DERIVED · 'A-01, A-03, A-04' — the very enumeration CR4-09 proved false. SP-040 · AUTHOR-PROPOSED · 'A-01'.
CR5-B03.consequence: T returns OPERATIVELY_DECIDED in this docket if and only if the author installed a clause settling the question. CR4-01 corrupted one comparison surface; this corrupts the FOUNDER'S DECISION SURFACE across six of eleven items. The founder's instinct that this could matter more than CR4-01 is upheld.
CR5-B03.aggravating: The author's own exculpatory sentence cited 'SP-019's fact set' as a non-authored ground. SP-019 is AUTHOR-PROPOSED and its exhaustiveness was falsified by CR4-09 in the immediately preceding review.

publication_integrity.independently_reproduced: YES — the reviewer extracted the §16.4 fence itself (SHA-256 590b8eed…dc4a2), executed those exact bytes, and obtained SHIPPED_BYTES_EXECUTED IDENTICAL · PUBLISHED_EVIDENCE_MATCH IDENTICAL · PUBLICATION_INTEGRITY PASS, with the core block byte-identical to §16.5.

CR5_05_the_hole_is_already_occupied.finding: The published diff block is FALSE. It reports ROWS_ADDED 5 / ROWS_CHANGED 5; the actual run reports 9 / 13, matching §16.6's hand-written prose.
CR5_05_the_hole_is_already_occupied.author_verification: CONFIRMED by direct extraction and execution. Published: ROWS_ADDED 5 -> [SP-167…SP-171], ROWS_CHANGED 5 -> [SP-095, SP-151, SP-152, SP-155, SP-159]. Actual: ROWS_ADDED 9 -> [SP-167…SP-175], ROWS_CHANGED 13.
CR5_05_the_hole_is_already_occupied.cause: The author's regeneration loop filled the diff block only on its first pass; subsequent passes refreshed the core and verification blocks only. The block froze in a pre-SP-172 state and was published under the sentence 'Produced by extracting the §16.4 block from this file and running the extracted bytes against this file.'
CR5_05_the_hole_is_already_occupied.significance: This is CR4-03's exact defect class recurring INSIDE the mechanism built to prevent it, in the one region the author carved out of the comparison. A carve-out from an integrity check is where the next integrity defect lands. The author built the check, exempted a region, and committed the defect in the exempted region.

other_material_findings.CR5-01: SP-168 EXACTNESS fails — the clause defines invocation as a function of (element, prefix); §2.0.1 publishes a function of element alone. At `record` from idle, SP-160 step 1 halts evaluation before content, so SP-032's success clause, SP-022, SP-021, SP-024 and SP-162 are not engaged yet all five are named. Over-broad by five. SP-169's 'cannot honor' predicate is also undefined over vacuously-satisfied obligations, and the two admissible readings yield different failed sets for the same substrate.
other_material_findings.CR5-02: SP-167 scopes the requirement set by 'this document's SP-006 envelope'. SP-006 OCCURS ZERO TIMES in v0.5, v0.4 and v0.3 — CONFIRMED by the author: the single hit in v0.5 is that reference itself. The closure predicate of the entire repair is a dangling reference.
other_material_findings.CR5-03: The flagship demonstration is non-exact under SP-169. G′ must also fail SP-032; H′ must also fail SP-022 and SP-032. §2.0, FT-13, FT-16 and §18 all publish the two-element sets {SP-022} / {SP-024}.

other_material_findings.CR5-07: SP-175 falsifies §6.1 and FT-10; three `view` domains now coexist. CR4-10 is PARTIALLY_CLOSED, not closed.

It nearly published 'the shipped-bytes check misses an in-fence edit', which is false. (3) SP-091's 'for every required vector' is the founder's own text at pin 85:97, not an author addition. requested_next_action.primary: Authorise SP-R06, bounded to Cold Review 005, with CR5-B01 controlling. But see the caution below before doing so.
requested_next_action.the_caution: Three consecutive revisions have each closed the prior blocker and introduced or left a new one: SP-R04 closed CR3-B01 and shipped CR4-01; SP-R05 closed CR4-01's embodiment half and shipped CR5-B01/B02/B03. CR5-B03 in particular is not a defect in a mechanism but a defect in how this cascade decides what the founder has decided — and it was present in v0.3 and v0.4 unnoticed. Repairing it may require changing what T(A) ranges over, which no bounded repair mandate has yet authorised.
requested_next_action.the_question_that_may_precede_repair: Whether SP-168 can be completed at all. Completing it means declaring, for all ~111 clauses, which are invoked by which element — and CR5-B01's four constructions suggest the honest answer for several is 'this obligation is not element-indexed at all', which the failed-requirement-set representation cannot express. If so, clause-identity individuation is the wrong shape and no amount of table-filling repairs it.
